tickets.title: Crate Specification Foundation — Purpose, Non-goals, Compliance & Functional Requirements
tickets.background:
**Goal**: Establish the architectural foundation specification for the siprs crate — a single document (specs/P0-1.md, 807 lines, 53KB) that defines Purpose, Non-goals, Compliance Requirements, and 15 Functional Requirements (FR-01 through FR-15). This spec serves as the authoritative design reference that all 48 downstream implementation tickets (P0-P7 phases) trace their origin to. The spec is consumed by 17 test functions in tests/spec_validation.rs (1183 lines total) and must pass all assertion-based validation.

**Purpose**: Create P0-1.md as the specification artifact that documents RFC-ROOT §§1-6 with full N0002-N0008 node coverage. Each node corresponds to an RFC section: N0002=M20 Priority (§1a), N0003=Non-goals+Tauri (§2+§2.1), N0004=Terminology (§3), N0005=Compliance (§4), N0006=Versioning (§4.1), N0007=FR (§5), N0008=Module Structure (§6). The spec establishes the design baseline for phases P0-P7 and defines Contracts C001-C069 linking design provenance edges.

**Motivation**: Without a unified specification document, 48 implementation tickets across 8 phases (P0-P7) would reference scattered RFC sections without a single source of truth. The P0-1 spec eliminates ambiguity about crate scope (audio-only SIP via PJSIP), compliance constraints (MSRV 1.95, PJSIP 2.17), and functional boundaries (15 FRs, 8 non-goals), preventing architectural drift during multi-phase implementation. spec_validation.rs enforces cross-reference consistency at test time.

**Constraints**: (1) Spec must reference all 7 foundation nodes (N0002-N0008) from RFC-ROOT §§1-6 — each node maps to a spec section via content.contains() assertion. (2) Contracts C001-C069 must be verifiable through content assertions in spec_validation.rs — no runtime code paths needed. (3) Spec file format must be Markdown (.md) consumable by spec_validation.rs tests via std::fs::read_to_string(). (4) Must not introduce implementation code — P0-1 is spec-only deliverable; implementation begins at P0-3+ (RuntimeCommand), P0-4+ (SipError).
scope: specs/P0-1.md: CRATE-SPECIFICATION — New spec file documenting siprs crate foundation (807 lines, 53KB, Markdown)

CREATE: Write P0-1.md specification document with all 7 node references (N0002-N0008), 14 expanded contract definitions (C001-C069 with pre/post/invariant), 37 testUnit entries mapped to Contracts, Acceptance Criteria (3 categories), Boy Scout translatability plan, Investigation evidence summary from RFC-ROOT.md and spec_validation.rs

Author P0-1.md covering 12 mandatory sections: (1) Purpose (§1) audio-only multi-account SIP via PJSIP+tokio, (2) M20 Priority Map (§1a) 14 items P0-P3 with Q1:A-Q14:A cross-references, (3) Non-goals (§2) 8 excluded categories + Tauri boundary §2.1, (4) Terminology (§3) 7 domain terms: Client, Account, Call, Media Session, Source, Chunk Pair, Raw SIP Event, (5) Compliance (§4) MSRV 1.95, PJSIP 2.17 pin, 3 target OS triples (Windows x86_64, macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64), prebuilt-first strategy, (6) Versioning (§4.1) 0.x phase + 1.0+ semver, (7) 15 FRs as FR-01 through FR-15 (multi-account through Send+Sync), (8) Module Structure (§6) full tree diagram + single-crate rationale, (9) Contracts C001-C069 mappings to testUnit/assertion methods, (10) Acceptance Criteria (happy path: all tests pass + error case: missing file/node + edge case: partial FR count), (11) Boy Scout translatability plan with 5 improvement items, (12) Investigation evidence from RFC-ROOT.md, spec_validation.rs, Cargo.toml

BEFORE (P0-1 start): specs/ directory does NOT exist; no spec artifact exists for crate foundation. AFTER (P0-1 done): specs/P0-1.md exists with 50+ subsections covering all 7 RFC nodes, 14 contract definitions with test mappings, 37+ testUnit entries, and node references to N0002-N0008. All 17 spec_validation.rs tests pass (see Integration Tests).

None — P0-1 is a spec-only ticket; no public API changes (lib.rs declares only module declarations and re-exports from config/error/model/state — no functional types like SipClient, ClientConfig, etc. implemented yet)
None — no data schema defined at this stage (RuntimeCommand serialization is P0-3, SipError type is P0-4, ClientConfig struct is P0-7)

Cargo.toml: Already declares MSRV 1.95 via rust-version = "1.95", edition 2021, PJSIP version 2.17 via comments, autoexamples = false for spec-examples feature gate (P1-3). No config changes needed at P0-1.

None — no new dependencies introduced at P0-1. Cargo.toml already has tokio (sync/rt/time/macros), thiserror, tracing, cfg-if, zeroize(optional), serde(optional), serde_json from prior commits and pre-P0-1 ticket work.

Implementation code (src/lib.rs, src/client.rs, src/account.rs, src/call.rs, etc.) — P0-1 is spec-only; src/ module implementation files are not created by this ticket. The 47 existing src/ .rs files are spec/documentation-level (config/error/model/state modules).

Code implementation is deliberately out of scope because P0-1 is a specification foundation ticket per the mandatory TDD Red phase — the spec must be fully validated (17 tests passing) before any implementation work starts, preventing architectural drift. Implementation begins at P0-3 (RuntimeCommand & Command Serialization), P0-4 (Comprehensive Error Design), P0-5/P0-6/P0-7+ (core types like ClientConfig, SipClient, EventBus).
All 48 downstream tickets in phases P0-P7 (including P0-2/P0-3/P0-4/P1-2/P1-3/P1-4/P1-5/P2-2/P2-4/P2-5 with existing specs/ subdirectories)

Spec foundation — every downstream spec and implementation must reference P0-1.md as their baseline and must not contradict its definitions (non-goals list, compliance values, FR enumeration, scope boundaries)

Downstream tickets validate their spec content against P0-1.md via spec_validation.rs assertion tests. Contradictions to P0-1 definitions (e.g., claiming video scope, different MSRV, incorrect FR count) are flagged as acceptance criteria failures. Architectural drift is prevented by mandatory cross-reference validation per Contracts C001-C069.

testExceptions: Item: Specification-level documentation nodes have no executable test code; coverage is via cross-reference verification in spec_validation.rs (17 test functions, 1183 lines). Reason: Spec content assertions (P0-1 foundation definitions: purpose, non-goals, compliance constraints) cannot test runtime behavior because they are static design documents, not executable code — the spec IS the test artifact for P0-1. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — the assertion-based approach using content.contains() string matching in spec_validation.rs provides fully deterministic validation that IS testable and IS covered by 30+ UT entries. Spec validation is the correct architectural choice for a spec-only deliverable (per Supreme Law 1.1: deterministic features that are fundamentally untestable are architectural defects — spec content validation IS testable via assertion matching, so no defect exists). Alternative verification: All 17 spec_validation.rs test functions use deterministic string matching against the spec file content, providing exhaustive validation of node references and contract satisfaction.

Item: Contracts C001-C069 define graph edge relationships between RFC design nodes (provenance lines: N0001→N0007, N0002→N0001, etc.). Reason: These contracts express design provenance (e.g., "Purpose is implemented by functional requirements") which are dependency relationships between document sections and cannot test runtime code paths — the tests are design-level assertions. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — contract satisfaction IS verified by node reference assertions in spec_validation.rs (spec_references_n0007, spec_has_m20_priority_map, spec_has_non_goals, etc.). Cross-reference validation via assert!(content.contains("N0007")) is the appropriate mechanism for provenance contracts. Alternative verification: Each contract maps to one or more @verifies annotations on test functions, cross-referenced in the @verifies C001-C060 inline comments.

Item: Inbound edge contracts (C010, C014, C040, C053, C058, C060, C067) require spec files from future tickets (P1-4, P2-2, P2-4, P2-5) that do not exist at P0-1 time. Reason: These contracts validate that downstream ticket specs reference P0-1 foundation nodes (N0005-N0008) — but those target .md files are created in future phases (P1+, P2+). This cannot test at P0-1 time because the target files have not been created. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — verification is deferred to each downstream ticket's make pipeline where show-ticket-context --for-spec validates cross-references. The spec_references_inbound_contract_targets test at P0-1 validates that P0-1.md itself references all 4 target nodes (N0005-N0008) for future inbound contracts. Alternative verification: When a downstream ticket (e.g., P1-4) runs its make pipeline, spec_validation.rs tests are enabled by removing #[ignore] on the corresponding test functions, validating that the downstream spec references P0-1 foundation nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: HAPPY PATH: specs/P0-1.md exists (807 lines, 53KB), passes all 17 spec_validation.rs tests (spec_file_exists, spec_references_n*, spec_has_*, cargo_toml_has_correct_msrv, versioning_policy_config_struct_exists, spec_references_inbound_contract_targets), references all 7 foundation nodes (N0002-N0008) with matching RFC-ROOT sections, enumerates all 15 functional requirements (FR-01 through FR-15 documented with concrete behavior descriptions), documents all 8 non-goals and Tauri boundary, lists compliance requirements (MSRV 1.95, PJSIP 2.17, 3 OS targets). All 14 Contracts C001-C069 have precondition/postcondition/invariant mappings to testUnit entries. verify-make-contracts.js exits 0. enumerate-ticket-targets.js and validate-ticket-targets.js both exit 0.

ERROR CASE: Spec file missing causes `spec_file_exists` test to fail with `assert!(path.exists(), ...)` — path.exists() returns false. Missing node reference (e.g., omitting N0007) causes specific assertion failure with descriptive message ("spec must reference N0007"). Cargo.toml MSRV mismatch (rust-version different from 1.95) causes `cargo_toml_has_correct_msrv` to fail. Cross-node validation detects contradictory content — e.g., if spec claims video functionality, `spec_audio_only_scope` fails on `!content.contains("video-scope")`.

EDGE CASE: Spec file content partially valid (e.g., 13/15 FRs enumerated) triggers FR count assertion in `spec_has_functional_requirements` requiring >=10 (>=10 passes but ==15 is better). Priority map with fewer than 3 levels triggers assertion in `spec_has_m20_priority_map` requiring >=3 (priority_mentions >= 3). Empty spec content is rejected by content.contains() assertions. All boundary tests (FR count=15, OS count=3, non-goals count=8) use exact-count assertions where feasible.

(3) Verify 7 node references present in spec (N0002-N0008). (4) Run STUB enumeration: `node .claude/scripts/tickets/review/find-all-stubs.js src` and `node .claude/scripts/tickets/enumerate-ticket-targets.js --dir=. --ticket-key=P0-1 --tickets=Tickets.json`. - **Risks**: (1) Spec file may diverge from RFC-ROOT if RFC is updated without corresponding P0-1 update — mitigation: spec_validation.rs test enforces node references via content.contains() assertions, catching drift. (2) Contract-test mapping gap — if testUnit entries don't fully cover all 14 contracts, verify-make-contracts.js will fail at Step 6-1. (3) Inbound edge contracts (C010/C014/C040/C053/C058/C060/C067) from future tickets can't be verified at P0-1 time — deferred to each downstream ticket's make pipeline.
- **Caveats**: (1) P0-1 is a living document — it will be supplemented by downstream specs (P0-2 Versioning Policy, P0-3 RuntimeCommand, P0-4 SipError, P1-4 Test Strategy, P2-2 Build Strategy, P2-4 JWT Auth, P2-5 Layer 5 API) which add detail but must not contradict P0-1. (3) spec-examples feature gate in Cargo.toml is a [::STUB::] marker requiring resolution in P1-3 (N0050).
- **Open items**: (1) P0-1 does not yet define the full RFC node graph query integration — show-ticket-context --for-spec will add this at output time via dump-ticket-graph-commands.js. - **Future improvements**: (1) Add auto-generation of contract-to-test mapping when graph node IDs change (N0002-N0008→spec section mapping). (2) Add spec diff tool to detect P0-1 baseline violations in downstream PRs (e.g., FR-XX count change, MSRV deviation). (3) Integrate spec validation into CI gate via `make check-spec` target. === RFC-ROOT.md Structure (source: RFC-ROOT.md) ===
Complete design document with 7+ sections covering all foundation nodes:
- §1 Purpose: audio-only multi-account SIP client via PJSIP FFI bindings + Tokio async runtime
- §1a M20 Priority Map: 14 items across P0-P3 with Q1:A-Q14:A cross-references to design decisions
- §2 Non-goals: 8 excluded categories (SIP server, PBX, RTP stack, recording, GUI, persistence, billing, video)
- §2.1 Tauri boundary: siprs provides Rust native API only; Tauri ipc::Channel/JS is adapter responsibility

- §6 Module Structure: 26+ source files, single-crate with modular internal structure (api/, audio/, config/, error/, ffi/, model/, runtime/, state/, util/)
- §6.1 Crate split rationale: PJSIP FFI coupling, call/media inseparability, Tauri utility vs future siprs-server split

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
=== In-Scope Translatability Improvements ===

1. **spec_validation.rs — walkdir function renamed**: `walk_source_files_excluding_hidden` already renamed from previous `walkdir_without_hidden` (Boy Scout applied in prior start-ticket). Function name now reads as a verb phrase: "walk source files excluding hidden directories." Doc comment explains filtering logic (skip entries starting with `.`). This pattern is reusable by future tickets needing file-tree walking (P2-4 tauri boundary check).

2. **Spec file — Node cross-reference table**: P0-1.md includes a formatted node-to-section mapping table at the top of each section: N0002->§1a (M20 Priority), N0003->§2 (Non-goals), N0004->§3 (Terminology), N0005->§4 (Compliance), N0006->§4.1 (Versioning), N0007->§5 (FRs), N0008->§6 (Module Structure). Readers can trace requirements to RFC sections without reading the entire document — this is the spec-as-navigable-prose principle.

3. **Hardcoded values as named constants**: All magic values in test assertions are extracted into named Rust constants in spec_validation.rs: SPEC_PATH ("specs/P0-1.md"), MSRV 1.95 verified via Cargo.toml string match rather than inline literal repetition. The spec file itself documents MSRV, PJSIP version, OS count, FR count, and non-goals count as explicit enumerations rather than prose — making assertion logic transparent.

4. **Contract names as function-signature style**: Each contract precondition/postcondition/invariant in the spec is formatted as if they were function signatures: `precondition(input: PurposeScope) -> void`, `postcondition(output: SpecContent) -> NodeReferences`, `invariant(state: SpecDocument) -> AudioOnly`. This makes the contract-to-assertion mapping in test code transparent — @verifies C001 annotations on test functions directly reference contract IDs.

5. **Function-style test naming**: All 17 P0-1 test functions follow verb_noun naming: spec_file_exists, spec_references_n0007, spec_audio_only_scope, cargo_toml_has_correct_msrv — each reads as a command describing what behavior is validated, improving translation from test name back to requirement.

=== Out-of-Scope Observations (future ticket recommendations) ===
- tests/spec_validation.rs imports are organized by contract group (C001-C009 group, C010-C069 inbound group) but lack module-level `mod` separation. Consider extracting into test modules by contract cluster in a future refactoring pass when the file exceeds 1500 lines.

tickets.title: Versioning Policy Implementation
tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the authoritative versioning policy specification for the siprs crate — a single self-contained design document (specs/P0-2.md) that codifies the two-phase versioning strategy (0.x development phase and 1.0+ stable phase) defined in RFC-ROOT §4.1, along with helper functions for programmatic policy enforcement.

### Purpose
Provide a clear, enforceable policy that governs API compatibility expectations across the crate lifecycle. During 0.x development (pre-1.0), rapid iteration with breaking changes is permitted to accelerate stabilization. After 1.0, strict semver compliance protects downstream consumers from unexpected breakage. The policy serves as both documentation for humans (CHANGELOG.md) and a programmatic API for CI tooling (semver-checks integration in P2-2).

### Motivation
The siprs crate is at version 0.1.0 with a 48-ticket multi-phase implementation roadmap spanning P0-P7. Without an explicit versioning policy: (1) downstream consumers cannot predict when API breaks occur, (2) CI tooling cannot enforce semver compliance, (3) crate maintainers lack guidance on which changes require MAJOR vs MINOR vs PATCH bumps. Establishing the policy now, at the outset of the implementation phase, prevents confusion and miscommunication about API stability expectations throughout the development lifecycle.

### Constraints
(1) Versioning policy must be implementable as pure Rust code — no external dependencies for policy evaluation (semver parsing uses the semver crate optionally; core logic is dependency-free). (2) Policy must be fully unit-testable without PJSUA or tokio — plain #[test] functions only. (3) Policy must align with cargo semver conventions for eventual CI integration in P2-2. (4) Must not introduce unsafe code. (5) Must maintain backward compatibility with Cargo.toml version field parsing (std::env! or include_str! based).
scope: src/config/versioning_policy.rs — Version policy constants and enforcement helpers
0.x phase: breaking changes allowed with CHANGELOG notification, #[non_exhaustive] on SipEventPayload
1.0+: strict semver (MAJOR for breaking API changes, MINOR for backward-compatible additions, PATCH for fixes)
Security exception: critical fixes bypass MAJOR delay
Runtime behavior changes (timeouts, retries) are PATCH-level even in 1.0+

**Scope of changes (describe each change comprehensively):**
  - [File/module path] src/config/versioning_policy.rs
  - [Action: add/modify/remove/rename/refactor] MODIFY — replace stub Config struct with VersionPolicy struct, VersionPhase enum, ChangeKind enum, classify_change() and is_breaking_change_allowed() functions
  - [What specifically changes] pub struct Config {} stub → pub struct VersionPolicy { phase: VersionPhase } with constructor and accessors; add pub enum VersionPhase { Dev, Stable }; add pub enum ChangeKind { Major, Minor, Patch }; add pub fn classify_change(description: &str) -> Result<ChangeKind, VersionError>; add pub fn is_breaking_change_allowed(&self) -> bool; add pub fn is_changelog_required(&self, change: &ChangeKind) -> bool
  - [Before → After (behavior/signature)] Before: versioning_policy.rs contains `pub struct Config {}` with no methods. After: versioning_policy.rs exports VersionPolicy, VersionPhase, ChangeKind, VersionError types with full policy evaluation logic
  - [API contract change (if any)] New public types: VersionPolicy, VersionPhase, ChangeKind, VersionError. New public functions: VersionPolicy::new(), classify_change(), is_breaking_change_allowed(), is_changelog_required(), version_phase_from_semver()
  - [Data schema change (if any)] None — no data persistence involved
  - [Config/env change (if any)] None — version is read from cargo package version at compile time via env!()
  - [Dependency added/removed (if any)] Optional: semver crate for version string parsing if not using manual parsing

**Out of scope (items intentionally excluded, with justification):**
  - [Excluded item] CHANGELOG.md auto-generation or format validation
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] CHANGELOG is human-authored; is_changelog_required() provides boolean guidance but does not enforce format. Format enforcement is a CI concern deferred to P2-2.
  - [Excluded item] cargo semver-checks CI integration
  - [Why excluded — separate ticket / future phase / not applicable] Deferred to P2-2 (N0066 Semver Operations) which builds on P0-2's policy definitions

**Affected areas (components/systems impacted, even without direct modification):**
  - [Affected component] specs/P0-2.md — new spec file
  - [Nature of impact: API surface / documentation] Defines versioning policy as the crate's baseline; all downstream tickets must not contradict P0-2 versioning rules
  - [Corresponding change needed Y/N + details] Y — Create specs/P0-2.md spec file documenting full versioning policy with all template markers replaced
  - [Affected component] tests/spec_validation.rs — versioning_policy_config_struct_exists() test already written, references versioning_policy.rs Config struct
  - [Nature of impact: test validation] Spec validation test must pass once Config-like struct exists

tickets.title: RuntimeCommand Enum & Command Serialization
tickets.background:
### Goal
Establish the authoritative RuntimeCommand enum definition and MPSC serialization model for the siprs crate — the single input path through which all PJSUA operations (init, account management, calling, DTMF, shutdown) are serialized and dispatched to the reactor thread. This design ensures PJSUA thread-safety constraints are never exposed to crate consumers.

### Purpose
Provide a type-safe, Send+Sync-compatible command enum that (a) enumerates all PJSUA-facing operations as typed variants, (b) carries per-command oneshot reply channels for asynchronous result delivery, (c) is serializable through a single unbounded tokio::sync::mpsc channel, and (d) supports future extension via M20 feature-gated variants without breaking existing match arms.

### Motivation
PJSUA (PJSIP) is fundamentally not thread-safe — all API calls must execute on the same thread that initialized the library. Without an explicit serialization layer, consumers would need to manage PJSUA thread safety themselves, defeating the crate's safety promise. The RuntimeCommand+MPSC pattern encapsulates this constraint from the start: all 10 base operations (Initialize through Shutdown) plus 4 M20 operations are defined as enum variants, each carrying a oneshot reply channel. This is the foundational concurrency primitive that all higher-level APIs (P0-7 SipClient, P0-8 AccountConfig) will be built upon.

### Constraints
(1) Must use tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender for replies — no shared-state callback patterns. (2) Must achieve Send+Sync without requiring PJSUA types on the enum (PJSUA types are !Send). (3) Enum variants use type aliases for future types (ClientConfig, AccountConfig, AccountId, CallId, SipError, etc.) that will be defined in later tickets — the enum compiles as long as these types exist as minimal placeholder definitions. (4) M20 variants (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo, SubscribeAudio) must be feature-gated behind #[cfg(feature = "m20")]. (5) No unsafe code — the serialization model must be purely safe Rust.

[Alternative verification] CI runs cargo test --features m20 and cargo test (no flag) in separate jobs. Exception 2 — oneshot::Sender does not implement Debug: [Item] RuntimeCommand cannot derive Debug because tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<T> does not implement Debug. [Reason] This cannot test because Debug is an auto-trait that cannot be manually satisfied for a type containing oneshot::Sender — it is a Tokio API design choice that prevents leaking channel state, not a design defect in siprs. The absence of Debug does not affect correctness or testability of command variants. [Alternative verification] Implement a manual Display-like function that prints the variant discriminant name via std::mem::discriminant or a hand-written helper. tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】All RuntimeCommand variants carry exactly one oneshot::Sender for reply delivery. Every variant construction must supply the sender. No variant may be constructed without a valid reply channel.
- 【Invariant on error】Even when a reply Sender is dropped (receiver cancelled) before the command executes, the RuntimeCommand enum itself must not panic or corrupt. The drop behavior of oneshot::Sender is idempotent — send() on a closed channel simply returns Err. No error handling code in command dispatch should unwrap or assume the receiver is alive.
- 【Internal state invariant】RuntimeCommand is pub(crate) — not accessible outside the crate. No public API may expose a RuntimeCommand reference. The enum discriminants are matched exhaustively in the reactor dispatch loop (future P0-7); a match on RuntimeCommand variants must never use a catch-all `_` arm because the compiler's exhaustiveness check on sealed enums prevents missing a new variant.
- 【Boundary invariant】The Send+Sync auto-trait implementation of RuntimeCommand must be verified at compile time. If any variant field is changed to a !Send or !Sync type (e.g., raw PJSUA pointers), the compile-time assertion must fail immediately. This prevents accidental thread-safety violations when extending the enum.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] RuntimeCommand is a pure data enum with no logging responsibility. Logging of command dispatch belongs in the reactor layer (P0-7). This module is intentionally silent — no log/println/tracing calls should exist in command_serialization.rs outside of test code.
- [Metrics] No metrics are emitted from this file. The command dispatch latency metrics belong to the reactor (P0-7). This module carries only the type definitions.
- [Error tracking] No error tracking needed — enum construction is infallible. Type errors are caught at compile time. Reply channel errors (send failure due to dropped receiver) are handled by the caller at the reactor level.
- [Health check] No health check responsibility. The module defines types only; runtime health is the reactor's concern.

tickets.title: Comprehensive Error Design — SipError & M20 Command Error Handling
tickets.background:
N0016 defines SipError struct (kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id, retryable) and SipErrorKind enum. N0017 defines error design for M20 RuntimeCommands reusing existing SipErrorKind variants. Maps to src/error/error_design_siperror.rs and src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs.

### Goal
Implement the SipError struct and SipErrorKind enum as specified in §14 of RFC-ROOT, providing a unified error type for all siprs public APIs. Implement M20 RuntimeCommand error conversion functions that reuse existing SipErrorKind variants.

### Purpose
Centralize all SIP error handling into a single, well-typed error type with stable classification (SipErrorKind), native PJSUA error preservation (native_status: Option<i32>), domain context (account_id, call_id), and recoverability information (retryable: bool). This eliminates ad-hoc error string passing and enables systematic retry/fallback logic.

### Motivation
P0-3 (RuntimeCommand enum) depends on SipError for the SipReply<T> = oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> pattern. Without SipError, all MPSC reply channels would use String-based errors, losing type safety and classification. M20 commands (ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, GetAccountInfo) need error conversion but must NOT introduce new SipErrorKind variants to keep error handling exhaustive and manageable.

### Constraints
1. No new SipErrorKind variants for M20 commands — reuse InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError only. 2. thiserror v2 must be used for Error derive. 3. SipError must implement Send + Sync (oneshot channel requirement). 4. All types must be pub(crate) at minimum (internal crate usage). 5. Must compile with the existing Cargo.toml dependency set (thiserror = "2" already added). 6. AccountId and CallId types must be imported from crate::concurrency_contexts (stub types from P0-3) until P0-9 replaces them.

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] SipError.kind must always be a valid SipErrorKind variant — no invalid/uninitialized discriminant state. SipError.message must always be a valid UTF-8 String (not null, not uninitialized).
- [Error invariant] Even when SipError is constructed with native_status=None, account_id=None, call_id=None, the struct remains fully functional and Display/Debug produce valid output — no partial initialization state.
- [Internal state invariant] The retryable flag must be consistent with the SipErrorKind: once assigned, it must not be changed implicitly. The convenience constructors (invalid_state, not_found, internal_error) must set retryable according to the error classification table.
- [Boundary invariant] native_status field accepts the full i32 range (−2^31 to 2^31−1), including PJ_SUCCESS=0. account_id accepts the full u64 range (0 to 2^64−1). call_id accepts the full u64 range (0 to 2^64−1). message accepts any valid String length (0 to usize::MAX).
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] SipError creation should be logged at debug level when kind is recoverable (retryable=true), warn level for non-recoverable application errors, and error level for InternalInvariantBroken. Each log entry should include kind, message, native_status, account_id, call_id.
- [Metrics] Counters for each SipErrorKind variant created (total_error_count, error_by_kind) to detect error pattern shifts. Counter for M20 conversion invocations per command type (conf_connect_errors, conf_disconnect_errors, get_account_info_errors).
- [Error tracking] SipError Display format is designed to integrate with structured error reporting (tracing::error! or sentry). The kind field enables automated alert routing by error category.

tickets.investigation:
- [Architecture] RFC-ROOT §14 defines SipError as the unified error type for all siprs public APIs. SipError wraps: kind (SipErrorKind enum), message (human-readable), native_status (Option<i32> for PJSUA error codes), account_id/call_id (domain context), retryable (bool for recoverability).
- [Source evidence] src/error/error_design_siperror.rs: currently pub enum Error {} — complete stub (N0016). src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs: currently pub enum Error {} — complete stub (N0017). Both files have the Initial Design Artifact header with N0016/N0017 node IDs.
- [Source evidence] src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs lines 29-35: defines a stub pub(crate) struct SipError(pub(crate) String); with a STUB marker that says "Replace with use crate::error::SipError once P0-4 implements it." P0-4 explicitly resolves this.
- [Source evidence] src/concurrency_contexts/command_serialization.rs defines SipReply<T> = oneshot::Sender<Result<T, SipError>> (line 105). All RuntimeCommand variants use SipReply<T> in their reply fields. This confirms the dependency: P0-3 -> P0-4.
- [Dependency analysis] Cargo.toml already has thiserror = "2" (added by P0-3 as a STUB for P0-4). AccountId and CallId are stub types from P0-3; they will be replaced by real types from P0-9 (crate::model).
- [Pattern analysis] The RFC defines 22 SipErrorKind variants. M20 error conversion functions (convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error) must only produce InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError — no new variants allowed.
- [Retryable classification] RFC specifies retryable=true for recoverable errors (Timeout, Transport init, Registration, Auth, Invite, Media negotiation, ICE, NativeError). retryable=false for unrecoverable (InvalidConfig, InvalidState, AlreadyInitialized, NotInitialized, AccountNotFound, CallNotFound, MediaInitFailed, TlsFailed, SrtpFailed, AudioFormatUnsupported, AudioPipelineBroken, DtmfFailed, ChannelClosed, ShutdownInProgress, InternalInvariantBroken).

tickets.title: M20 NativeEvent Conversion — CallState, CallMediaState & RegistrationStateChanged
tickets.background:
N0021 defines complete NativeEvent to SipEventPayload mapping table. N0022 provides pjsip_inv_state to CallState mapping and media_status conversion. N0023 defines the RegistrationStateChanged processing via RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo pattern. Maps to src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs, src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs, src/state/m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs.

### Goal
Implement three pure conversion functions + one data struct that bridge PJSIP NativeEvent callbacks to the siprs SipEventPayload event system: (1) convert_native_event_to_payload in m20_native_event_conv.rs — maps all 12 NativeEvent variants to Option<SipEventPayload> with P0/P1/P2 priority tiers; (2) convert_call_state + convert_call_media_state in m20_callstate_mapping.rs — maps pjsip_inv_state values 0-4 and pjsua_call_media_status values 0-4 to SipEventPayload; (3) AccountInfoSnapshot struct + RegistrationStateChanged flow in m20_registr_cmd_pat.rs — bridges RegistrationStateChanged through RuntimeCommand::GetAccountInfo.

### Purpose
These conversion functions are the bridge between the PJSIP C callback layer (NativeEvent) and the typed Rust event system (SipEventPayload). Without them, PJSIP events like registration state changes, call state transitions, media state changes, and DTMF digits would remain as opaque C structs and never reach the application layer as typed, inspectable Rust events. The CONNECTING state discrimination (Trying vs Ringing) is essential for correct call-progress UI.

### Motivation
M20 phase requires P0 NativeEvent events (Registration/CallState/CallMediaState/DTMF) to be functional for integration testing. These are the minimum events needed to verify end-to-end SIP call flows in tests. The current stub files (pub enum State {}) must be replaced with real implementations.

### Constraints
(1) FFI boundary: pjsip_inv_state and media_status are C integer enums — Rust code matches on documented constant values, not PJSIP types. (2) Stateless pure functions: converters must not hold mutable state; CONNECTING discrimination receives previous_state as parameter. (3) No EventBus dependency in this layer — conversion layer returns Option<SipEventPayload>; publish responsibility lives upstream in Reactor (P0-5/P0-7). (4) All 12 NativeEvent variants must be matched exhaustively — no wildcard _ arm.

tickets.title: M20 DtmfSentInfo Two-Phase Design
tickets.background:
- Goal: Implement DtmfSentInfo struct, SentDtmfError enum, and establish the two-phase DTMF send semantics (immediate command accept + async DtmfSent event) in src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs
- Purpose: SipClient::send_dtmf() callers need a way to distinguish command-queued (synchronous return) from actual DTMF-sent or failed (asynchronous DtmfSent event). Without two-phase design, callers cannot tell whether DTMF digits were really sent or merely queued.
- Motivation: P0 priority per M20 implementation map. Required by zasso voice communication for reliable DTMF feedback during calls. The 500ms timeout fallback ensures no event is lost even if PJSIP callback is unavailable.
- Constraints: No FFI bindings exist yet (pjsua_call_dial_dtmf not accessible from Rust). SentDtmfError uses simulated pj_status_t (PJ_EINVALIDOP_SIM pattern). SipEventPayload::DtmfSent variant is not yet added (deferred to P5-1). Must be self-contained in single file following P1-2 pattern.

# Investigation Evidence for P1-3

## RFC Design (RFC-ROOT.md §20)
- DtmfSentInfo struct defined with fields: method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, status:Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status:Option<pj_status_t>
- SentDtmfError enum: PjsipError(pj_status_t), Timeout
- Two-phase design: send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) immediately (command accepted by Reactor), DtmfSent event fires async when PJSIP actually sends or timeout occurs
- Priority Q2:A: DTMF two-phase (return value=command accepted, DtmfSent=send complete)
- Priority Q14:A: DtmfSent: PJSIP callback absent => 500ms timeout fallback
- 500ms default timeout via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

tickets.title: M20 Dual Client PJSIP Callback Routing
tickets.background:
N0038 defines single Reactor + EventBus split for multiple SipClient instances sharing PjsuaBackend singleton. Account_id-based event dispatch. Maps to src/state/m20_dual_client_routing.rs (no direct file in Dirs-Tree, grouped with Dual Client routing logic).

### Goal
Implement the Dual Client callback routing mechanism — Reactor::dispatch_event() that routes SipEvents to the correct client's EventBus based on account_id, supporting multiple SipClient instances sharing a single PjsuaBackend singleton.

### Purpose
Enable multiple SipClient instances (dual/multi-client) to coexist in the same process by routing PJSIP callbacks to the correct client's EventBus, maintaining event isolation between clients while sharing the single PjsuaBackend singleton (pjsua_init() once-per-process constraint).

### Motivation
The M20 phase requires dual-client integration tests (call rejection, call transfer) where two logical SipClient instances share the same PjsuaBackend. Without account_id-based routing, events from one client's account would leak to the other client's EventBus, breaking isolation. The P2 priority reflects that single-client operation works via default EventBus — this is the multi-client routing extension.

### Constraints
PjsuaBackend is a OnceLock singleton — cannot be instantiated twice per process. global_runtime() returns a single Arc<Reactor> — no per-client Reactor. EventBus is per SipClient, registered in the shared Reactor. Routing key is AccountId(u64) — events without account_id (None) go to default EventBus. Call events (CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged) carry call_id only, not acc_id — reactor must maintain call_id→account_id mapping. No new crate dependencies beyond tokio (broadcast channel) already in Cargo.toml.
scope: Reactor dispatch_event() logic: account_id-based EventBus routing
Multiple SipClient EventBus registration in Reactor
Default EventBus for non-account-specific events
DualClientContext test utility pattern

**Scope of changes:**
  - Path: `src/state/m20_dual_client_routing.rs` (new file) — Dual Client routing logic: dispatch_event, register/unregister_client_event_bus, call_id→account_id mapping table.
  - Action: **add** — create m20_dual_client_routing.rs as new state sub-module.
  - Detail: Implement Reactor::dispatch_event(SipEvent) → routes to correct EventBus by account_id; Reactor::register_client_event_bus(EventBus, Vec<AccountId>) → adds mapping; Reactor::unregister_client_event_bus(EventBus) → removes all AccountId mappings for that bus; CallEventRouter: HashMap<CallId, AccountId> for call_id→account_id resolution.
  - Before → After: Before — no dual-client routing (single default EventBus only). After — Reactor holds default_event_bus + HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> routing table; each SipClient's events are isolated by account_id.
  - API change: Reactor gains pub(crate) dispatch_event(), register_client_event_bus(), unregister_client_event_bus() methods. EventBus gains pub(crate) new() constructor and publish/subscribe control_channel methods.
  - Schema change: None — no data schema change. New internal HashMap data structures only.
  - Config change: None — routing is automatic based on SipClient registration order.
  - Dependency: No new crate dependencies. Uses existing tokio::sync::broadcast and std::collections::HashMap.

**Out of scope:**
  - PjsuaBackend singleton implementation — handled by P0-5 (Reactor) and P0-6 (Backend). P1-4 assumes it exists.
  - Full EventBus implementation (broadcast channel, subscribe, Receiver) — handled by P1-0. P1-4 defines the routing table and dispatch logic that calls EventBus::publish().
  - SipClient facade — handled by P0-7. P1-4 defines the registration point where SipClient registers its EventBus in the Reactor.
  - DualClientContext full test utility implementation — handled by P2-2. P1-4 defines the DualClientContext struct skeleton and constructor pattern.

**Affected areas:**
  - Component: Reactor (P0-5) — P1-4 defines the dispatch_event routing method that Reactor::process_native_event() calls after conversion.
  - Nature of impact: Performance — dispatch_event adds HashMap lookup per SipEvent. O(1) average case, no new allocations. Security — event isolation between SipClient instances prevents cross-client event leaks.
  - Response: Reactor (P0-5) must call Reactor::dispatch_event() after NativeEvent→SipEventPayload conversion. No other components need modification.

acceptanceCriteria: Multiple SipClient instances share PjsuaBackend singleton safely — No duplicate pjsua_init(), no data race on backend state.

Events are routed to correct Client EventBus by account_id — Registration events (with acc_id) route to the owning client's bus. Call events (with call_id) resolve account_id via call→account mapping then route correctly.

**[Happy path]** Two SipClients (A, B) registered with distinct AccountIds. Dispatch event for account_a → only client_a's EventBus receives it. Dispatch event for account_b → only client_b's EventBus receives it.
**[Error case]** Dispatch event for unknown AccountId (no client registered for that id) → falls back to default EventBus (first registered client's bus). No panic, no event loss.

**[Edge case]** Non-account event (account_id=None) → published to default EventBus only. Never published to all client buses. Non-account event with empty client_event_buses map → still handled by default EventBus.

contracts.precondition: FFI layer and SipBackend exist — NativeEvent enum (m20_native_event_conv.rs) is constructable with valid AccountId and CallId; PjsuaBackend singleton (OnceLock) has been initialized via pjsua_init(); AccountId(CallId) newtypes (command_serialization.rs) implement Copy + Clone + PartialEq + Eq for use as HashMap keys in the Reactor routing table.
contracts.postcondition: Dual Client callback routing specified — Reactor::dispatch_event(SipEvent) routes the event to the correct client EventBus based on event.meta.account_id match against a HashMap<AccountId, ClientEventBus> routing table; non-account events (meta.account_id=None) route to the default EventBus only; unknown account_ids fall back to default EventBus; no event is published to multiple client buses simultaneously.
contracts.invariant: Single Reactor + EventBus split — global_runtime() returns the same Arc<Reactor> instance for all SipClient instances; Reactor owns exactly one default_event_bus: EventBus and a client_event_buses: HashMap<AccountId, EventBus>; the total number of EventBus instances equals 1 (default) + N (registered clients); event delivery is at-most-once per client (no broadcast to all).

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】Reactor's default_event_bus must always be initialized before any client EventBus registration (PjsuaBackend singleton must exist). All client EventBus registrations must carry at least one AccountId. Reactor routing table HashMap<AccountId, EventBus> must remain in sync with active SipClient instances.
- 【Invariant on error】On dispatch_event failure (e.g., broadcast channel send error), the Reactor must not panic — the error is logged and the event is dropped. The routing table is never corrupted by failed publishes. The default EventBus must always accept events even if all client buses are dropped.
- 【Internal state invariant】The Reactor holds exactly one default_event_bus: EventBus and N client_event_buses: HashMap<AccountId, EventBus>. No two entries in client_event_buses map to the same EventBus instance pointer (distinct clones). The Reactor instance is behind Arc<Reactor> (shared ownership, not cloned per client).
- 【Boundary invariant】AccountId values range from 0 to u64::MAX. The routing table must handle all values without overflow or wrapping. An empty client_event_buses map (no clients registered) must still function — all events route to default EventBus.

(5) Implement CallEventRouter (HashMap<CallId, AccountId>) for call_id→account_id resolution. (6) Implement DualClientContext test skeleton with PjsuaBackend singleton sharing pattern. (7) Write unit tests for all routing paths. (8) Add m20_dual_client_routing to state/mod.rs.
- 【Risks】Dependency on P0-5 (Reactor implementation) — if Reactor API differs from current RFC design, dispatch_event integration point may need rework. Dependency on P1-0 (EventBus implementation) — if EventBus uses a different publish interface than tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender, the dispatch_event logic may need adjustment. CallId→AccountId mapping requires P0-9 (AccountId/CallId newtypes) to be non-stub.
- 【Caveats】The dual-client routing spec (this ticket) defines the routing logic abstractly. The concrete Reactor integration (calling dispatch_event from process_native_event) belongs to P0-5, not P1-4. The EventBus::publish() call inside dispatch_event is the boundary — P1-4 calls it, P1-0 provides it. Call events carry call_id, not acc_id — routing these requires maintaining a call_id→account_id mapping that is updated when accounts create calls.

Confirm: does this mean the Reactor borrows the first client's bus, or creates its own? Resolution: Reactor creates its own default_event_bus at initialization time; first SipClient's registration adds its accounts to the routing table but does not replace the default.

EventBus health monitoring — automatic unregistration when a client's EventBus receiver is dropped. Priority routing — some event types (e.g., TransportState) could be broadcast to all clients. Federation with call_id routing across accounts sharing the same SIP domain.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- **dispatch_event function naming**: Name the main routing function `dispatch_event_to_correct_bus` (reads as a verb phrase: "dispatch event to the correct bus"), not `route` or `handle_dispatch`. Internal helper functions named as verb phrases: `resolve_client_bus(account_id) -> Option<&EventBus>`, `route_to_default_or_client(event, maybe_bus)`.
- **Variable naming as domain concepts**: Use `routing_table: HashMap<AccountId, EventBus>` instead of `buses` or `map`. Use `call_owner: HashMap<CallId, AccountId>` instead of `call_map`. Use `default_event_bus` instead of `default` or `main`.
- **One function one responsibility**: dispatch_event does one thing — look up account_id in routing table and call publish on the correct bus. Registration/unregistration are separate methods. CallEventRouter is a separate struct with its own methods (register_call, resolve_account_for_call, unregister_call). No function exceeds 15 lines.
- **Hardcoded value extraction**: No hardcoded channel capacities, timeouts, or magic numbers in routing logic. Extract `DEFAULT_BROADCAST_CHANNEL_CAPACITY: usize = 256` as a named constant.
- **No error swallowing**: dispatch_event returns `Result<(), RoutingError>` where RoutingError has variants: `UnknownAccount { account_id }`, `BusClosed { account_id }`. The caller (Reactor) logs and drops on error — the dispatch itself never silently swallows.
- **Existing code outside scope**: No refactoring needed in existing files (m20_native_event_conv.rs, m20_callstate_mapping.rs) — they are already translatable. The `m20_dual_client_routing.rs` is new code built to translatability standards from the start.

tickets.title: SRTP Specification & Transport Reconnection Policy
tickets.background:
N0042 defines SrtpPolicy enum (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory), feature-gated by srtp feature flag, and transport reconnection strategy for UDP/TCP/TLS. Maps to src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs.

### Goal
Define the SrtpPolicy enum and ReconnectPolicy struct as foundational config types consumed by AccountConfig (P4-1), TransportConfig (P4-2), and PJSIP FFI layer (P4-5). Establish the feature-gating pattern for SRTP and the backoff-based reconnection parameters for UDP/TCP/TLS transports.

### Purpose
Provide type-safe SRTP policy selection (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory) with compile-time feature gating, and a configurable reconnection backoff policy that prevents reconnect storms while ensuring timely recovery — both are prerequisites for secure and resilient SIP communication.

### Motivation
SRTP support is required for P2P encrypted media (Asterisk/3CX interop targets list SRTP as mandatory in RFC-ROOT §Interoperability Matrix). Transport reconnection with backoff is essential for mobile/nomadic use where network interruptions are frequent. These types must be defined early as they are dependencies of AccountConfig (P4-1), TransportConfig (P4-2), and the validation pipeline (P4-7).

### Constraints
- SrtpPolicy::Mandatory/Optional must be #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] gated — no runtime fallback for missing libsrtp2
- ReconnectPolicy must remain transport-type agnostic (same struct for UDP/TCP/TLS) — per-transport specialization belongs in the FFI layer (P4-5)
- Backoff parameters must saturate at max_delay to prevent unbounded wait; jitter_ratio must be bounded [0.0, 1.0] for deterministic behavior
- No external dependencies added — uses only std::time::Duration and std::f32::consts

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] SrtpPolicy enum MUST have exactly 3 variants: Disabled (unconditional), Optional (srtp-feature-gated), Mandatory (srtp-feature-gated). ReconnectPolicy fields MUST satisfy: base_delay > 0, max_delay >= base_delay, jitter_ratio in [0.0, 1.0] after validation.
- [Error invariant] Even when validation fails (base_delay = 0, max_delay < base_delay, jitter_ratio out of range), the ReconnectPolicy struct must not panic or exhibit undefined behavior — invalid values are reported via Result::Err, never via panic or silent corruption.
- [Internal state invariant] compute_backoff(attempt) MUST return Duration in range [base_delay * (1 - jitter_ratio), max_delay] — minimum is base_delay with negative jitter, maximum is always capped at max_delay regardless of attempt count. jitter_ratio=0.0 produces deterministic delay.
- [Boundary invariant] SrtpPolicy serde roundtrip MUST preserve variant identity across serialization and deserialization (core::fmt::Debug + serde roundtrip for all 3 variants). ReconnectPolicy max_delay MUST be representable as Duration (max ~2^64-1 nanoseconds, ~584 years).
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] #[tracing::instrument] on ReconnectPolicy::validate() and compute_backoff() — log at info level on validation failure; log at debug level for backoff computation result (attempt, computed delay). Use tracing::field to annotate spans with attempt count and delay value.
- [Metrics] transport_reconnects_total counter (increment on each reconnect attempt) — field defined in RFC-ROOT §34.2. Gated behind #[cfg(feature = "metrics")]. The histogram of reconnect durations is handled by P4-5 FFI layer, not this ticket.
- [Error tracking] Validation errors from ReconnectPolicy::validate() are returned via Result::Err — caller (P4-7 Config Validation) is responsible for error tracking. No direct error aggregation in this module.
- [Health check] ReconnectPolicy and SrtpPolicy are passive configuration types with no runtime background activity — no health check endpoint needed at this layer. Runtime health check (P4-5 FFI layer) monitors transport connection states and reports via SipEvent::TransportDisconnected.
tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] 1) Define SrtpPolicy enum with Disabled/Optional/Mandatory: add #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] on Optional/Mandatory variants 2) Define ReconnectPolicy struct with pub fields 3) Implement ReconnectPolicy::{new, default, validate, compute_backoff} 4) Add srtp_transport_reconnect to config/mod.rs pub mod + pub use 5) Run cargo test with both feature combinations
- [Risks] cfg_eval for serde derive on feature-gated enum variants may require cfg_attr ordering care — #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(Serialize, Deserialize))] on the enum itself works correctly with per-variant #[cfg(...)] on individual variants (serde handles missing variants gracefully). Test serde roundtrip for each variant individualy.
- [Caveats] Duration arithmetic in compute_backoff must avoid overflow — (attempt + 1) as f64 for delay multiplier should use checked arithmetic; Duration::mul_f64 on Duration::MAX (~2^64 ns) times 1.0 is safe. jitter_ratio=0.0 produces deterministic output; jitter_ratio>0.0 uses pseudo-randomness from std (not cryptographically secure).
- [Open items] SrtpImplementation enum (SdesSrtp, DtlsSrtp) is owned by P2-1 (ClientCapabilities), not this ticket — confirm cross-reference when both tickets are implemented. SrtpPolicy→pjsua_acc_config.srtp_opt mapping belongs to P4-5.
- [Future improvements] Consider adding ReconnectPolicy multiplier (non-exponential backoff factor) for custom growth curves. Consider TruncatedExponentialBackoff variant for industry-standard capped exponential. Consider adding ReconnectPolicy::reset() to reset attempt counter after successful connection.
